# Exact support erosion and a quantitative middle-simplex neighborhood

This is an actual compatibility bound, retaining both endpoint bodies.
It gives an exact finite formula for the simplex support relaxation of
B subset T intersect (2K minus A), and then excludes an explicit
neighborhood of the ordinary simplex K=-T in the small-A bad-source
branch. It makes no assertion that an arbitrary middle body lies in
that neighborhood.

## 1. The actual support erosion in every dimension

Let d>=1, let v_1,...,v_(d+1) form a full-rank positive circuit
normalized by sum v_i=0, and let

    T={x: v_i.x<=1 for every i}, V=|T|.

Let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies with B subset T and
(A+B)/2 subset K. Define ACTUAL support values

    alpha_i=h_A(-v_i), t_i=h_K(-v_i),
    c_i=(1+2t_i-alpha_i)/(d+1).                    (1)

Midpoint containment implies, for every x in B and every i,

    v_i.x>=alpha_i-2t_i.

Indeed h_A(-v_i)+h_B(-v_i)<=2h_K(-v_i).
Consequently B lies in the actual necessary enclosure

    E=T intersect {x: v_i.x>=alpha_i-2t_i for all i}. (2)

If any c_i<=0, E has zero d-volume: in simplex barycentric
coordinates lambda_i=(1-v_i.x)/(d+1), it requires lambda_i<=0
or an impossible negative bound. In particular such support data
cannot admit a full-dimensional B.

If every c_i>0, the following EXACT volume identity holds:

    |E|/V=
      sum_(J subset {1,...,d+1}) (-1)^|J|
           (1-sum_(j in J)c_j)_+^d.              (3)

Here x_+=max(x,0), and the empty subset contributes one. To prove
it, use the barycentric simplex lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1.
For a fixed nonempty J, the event lambda_j>c_j for every j in J
is empty up to null faces if sum_J c_j>=1. Otherwise translate
those barycentric coordinates down by c_j and scale all remaining
mass by 1-sum_J c_j. The resulting simplex has volume ratio
(1-sum_J c_j)^d. Boundaries have d-volume zero. Finite
inclusion-exclusion over the d+1 violated coordinate bounds proves
(3) exactly. The same proof covers c_i>=1 without modification.

Thus |B|<=|E| with the explicit right side (3). No independent
replacement of a slice by a desired density is made.

If K itself is the aligned simplex {v_i.x>=-t_i}, then E is
EXACTLY T intersect (2K minus A), where

    2K minus A={x: x+A subset 2K}.

Therefore whenever E is full dimensional, it is the maximum-volume
possible B subset T compatible with these actual A and K, and that
maximum is attained by B=E. Requiring additional B facet contacts
can only shrink the admissible class; no contact is inferred from
the volume formula alone. For arbitrary K, (2) is a proved outer
relaxation of the true erosion, not an asserted equality.

All arguments take place in the continuous fiber space. A common
invertible continuous coordinate change scales all fiber volumes by
the same determinant and preserves the normalized formula relative
to V. Integer coordinates and their lattice are unaffected.

## 2. A planar bound from a small support excess

Now d=2, so V=9/2 in the canonical coordinates
v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1). Assume every A cut
v_i.x=-1 is proper. Then alpha_i>1.

Suppose, for some 0<=eta<=1/2, that the ACTUAL middle support
values satisfy

    t_i<=1+eta for every i.                       (4)

By (1), c_i<(2+2eta)/3. The simultaneous larger barycentric
bounds c_*=(2+2eta)/3 have disjoint violation events: since
c_*>=2/3, two violated coordinates would have sum greater than
one. Formula (3), or direct removal of the three corner triangles,
therefore gives

    b/V < f(eta),
    f(eta)=1-(1-2eta)^2/3.                        (5)

Here b=|B|. The inequality is strict. For eta<1/2 the actual
c_i are each strictly below c_*<1, so at least one strictly larger
corner cap is removed from the reference intersection by a positive
area: choose that barycentric coordinate just below c_* but above
its actual c_i, and split the remaining mass equally between the
other two coordinates. Both are strictly below c_*, so a small
relative open neighborhood is still in the reference intersection.
For eta=1/2,
each actual c_i<1 similarly removes a positive corner cap, giving
b<V=f(1/2)V. If one actual c_i<=0, there is no full-dimensional
B at all, as already observed.

This proof needs only actual support excess (4). It does not assume
that K is itself a triangle, that its facets are parallel to those
of T, or that the support relaxation equals the true erosion.

## 3. An explicit excluded sandwich neighborhood

Suppose in addition that

    (1-eta)(-T) subset K subset (1+eta)(-T),
    a<b/32, k<=a+b,                               (6)

where a=|A|, k=|K|. The outer inclusion gives (4), while the inner
one gives k>=(1-eta)^2 V. The two area assumptions give

    b>(32/33)k>=(32/33)(1-eta)^2 V.

This contradicts (5) whenever

    (32/33)(1-eta)^2 >=1-(1-2eta)^2/3,

equivalently

    5-54eta+38eta^2>=0.                           (7)

In particular all (6) are impossible for

    0<=eta<=eta_*= (27-sqrt(539))/38.              (8)

The smaller root eta_* is positive and less than 1/2; the quadratic
is nonnegative from zero to that root. Strictness in both (5) and
the lower b bound excludes equality at eta=eta_* too. No limit or
numerical root selection is being used.

In the planar proper-A, zero-B critical-cap configuration, the
condition k<=a+b in (6) is automatic under a bad-source bound
Q<=2(a+k+b)/9. The three middle traces cover the whole plane.
One therefore contains the ordinary centroid of K; the ordinary
Grunbaum inequality makes its middle cap at least 4k/9. Its full
mixed cap has mass Q, so Q>=4k/9. Combining these two inequalities
gives k<=a+b. Thus (8) is a concrete neighborhood exclusion in the
previously proved a<b/32 branch; no globally deepest source or
ordinary centroid membership in the mixed set is being presumed.

More generally one may replace the inner inclusion in (6) by the
single ACTUAL area lower bound k>=(1-xi)V. Then (4), a<b/32,
and k<=a+b force

    xi>1-(33/32)f(eta)
       =5/16-(11/8)eta+(11/8)eta^2.              (9)

The strict inequality follows from the strict bound (5) together
with b>32k/33. It is useful when an ordinary geometric argument
controls the middle area but not an entire inner simplex.

## 4. The actual thin-triangle warning is far from compatible

The actual A triangle in Section 3 of
`candidate fcbc840f56d4b6b6`
has support values

    alpha_1=101/100,
    alpha_2=alpha_3=899/200.

For K=-T, all t_i=1. Hence c_2=c_3=(3-899/200)/3<0.
Its necessary enclosure (2) is empty. More quantitatively, if a
middle body satisfies t_2,t_3<=1+eta, compatibility already fails
whenever

    eta<=299/400,

because then 1+2t_i-alpha_i<=0 for i=2,3. Thus those real A and K
can satisfy the section/ray screen and the ordinary A profile while
being decisively incompatible with ANY full-dimensional B subset T.
This uses actual support values of the same A; no formal section
array is mistaken for an actual endpoint enclosure.

The support-volume formula (3) can be applied with the actual,
unequal alpha_i and t_i, preserving additional information that the
single eta bound discards. The note proves no general control of
those support values from cap fractions alone and does not assert
that all remaining configurations lie in the excluded neighborhood.

## 5. A shape-free support-simplex deficit in the small-A branch

For arbitrary K define its ACTUAL aligned outer simplex

    K_out={x: v_i.x>=-h_K(-v_i) for every i},
    k_out=|K_out|, kappa_d=|T intersect (-T)|/|T|.

It is a bounded full-dimensional simplex containing K. Applying the
already proved and independently audited all-dimensional aligned
simplex theorem in
`candidate eb88c1c4c388daab`
to K_out gives

    b<kappa_d k_out.                               (10)

This theorem applies because the actual midpoint inclusion into K
implies inclusion into K_out and all A cuts remain proper. Its
strict inequality follows from their strict support excess. This
step invokes the archived proved theorem, not a new copy of its
symmetrization proof.

If a<b/32 and k<=a+b, then

    theta:=k/k_out <(33/32)kappa_d.                (11)

Indeed k<=a+b<(33/32)b<(33/32)kappa_d k_out.
For d=2, kappa_2=2/3, and hence

    |K|/|K_out|<11/16.                            (12)

The value kappa_2 follows either from (3) at c_i=2/3 or by
subtracting three disjoint corner triangles of relative area 1/9
from T. The bad-source condition makes k<=a+b automatic as proved
in Section 3. Thus every actual middle body filling at least 11/16
of its aligned support triangle is excluded in this small-A branch,
regardless of its shape, smoothness, or a particular sandwich.

The earlier archive proves <6/7 for arbitrary planar bad-source
configurations. Formula (12) is the stricter consequence retaining
the separate a<b/32 hypothesis. No converse deriving a lower bound
on theta from ordinary cap fractions is asserted here.
